papers.title: Integrative single-cell and machine learning analysis identifies a tumor doubling time-related prognostic signature and therapeutic targets in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity and diverse clinical outcomes, partly influenced by HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. Although tumor doubling time (TDT) reflects tumor growth kinetics and has prognostic relevance, its molecular basis in HNSCC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative single-cell and machine learning analyses to identify a prognostic signature based on tumor doubling time (TDT) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), revealing potential therapeutic targets. The findings link TDT-related molecular features to patient outcomes, offering a new tool for risk stratification and treatment guidance.

papers.title: A systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for single-cell and spatial RNA-seq nanopore long reads data.
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing plays a crucial role in transcriptomic complexity, yet remains difficult to resolve at the single-cell level due to the limitations of short-read technologies. Coupling single-cell with long-read sequencing offers full-length transcript coverage, enabling more accurate isoform detection. Diverse computational tools tailored for single-cell and spatial long-read transcriptomics have been developed. To compare the effectiveness of these approaches, we generated paired short-read and Nanopore long-read single-cell datasets, tailored for benchmarking bioinformatics tools. We e
papers.summary: This study presents a systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for analyzing single-cell and spatial RNA-seq data generated with Nanopore long-read sequencing. By generating paired short-read and long-read datasets, the authors evaluate the performance of various computational tools for isoform detection and quantification, providing guidance for researchers in this emerging field.

papers.title: Fishing with two lines: a hybrid approach to spatial transcriptomics discovery.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics faces a trade-off between the number of genes assayed and depth of per-gene sensitivity. We developed a "dual-chemistry" method that combines the high sensitivity of a 10x Genomics Xenium V1 custom panel (up to 480 genes) with the broad coverage of the Prime 5K panel (5,001 genes) on a single tissue section. This involved co-hybridizing Prime and V1 probes and sequentially running the V1 and Prime decoding chemistries. Applied to a human lung tissue microarray, we observed high concordance between the V1 and Prime chemistries when run independently (on serial sections)
papers.summary: This paper introduces a hybrid spatial transcriptomics approach that combines two different probe chemistries on the same tissue section, allowing researchers to capture both high sensitivity for a targeted gene set and broad genome-wide coverage. The method was validated on human lung tissue, showing high concordance between the two chemistries, and offers a practical solution to the trade-off between gene number and detection depth in spatial transcriptomics.

papers.title: MZB1 marks a B-cell-associated stromal-immune microenvironment in cervical squamous cell carcinoma: a multi-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) is a common gynecologic malignancy with a heterogeneous tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). The role of MZB1, a B-cell-specific molecular chaperone, in CSCC remains poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics analysis to characterize the role of MZB1 in cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC), finding that MZB1 marks a distinct B-cell-associated stromal-immune microenvironment. The results suggest MZB1 could serve as a biomarker or therapeutic target in CSCC.

papers.title: A Multi-omics Regulated Cell Death Framework Defines Immune Phenotypes and Guides Precision Therapy in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is molecularly and immunologically heterogeneous, contributing to variable treatment response. Because regulated cell death (RCD) intersects with tumor metabolism, immune regulation, and therapeutic susceptibility, we built an RCD-centered framework for CRC stratification. Multi-cohort transcriptomic data were used to infer RCD subtypes with non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) and non-negative least squares (NNLS). Genomic, bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, and spatial transcriptomic datasets were integrated to characterize subtype-associated biology. Machine-learn
papers.summary: This study develops a multi-omics framework for colorectal cancer (CRC) stratification based on regulated cell death (RCD) patterns, integrating transcriptomic, genomic, single-cell, and spatial data to define distinct immune phenotypes. The framework identifies RCD subtypes with differential treatment susceptibility, offering a potential guide for precision therapy in CRC.

papers.title: SPAE: Deciphering Cell Cycle Dynamics and Cell States in Single-cell RNA-seq Data.
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology have enabled the investigation of gene expression changes at the single-cell level, particularly for elucidating the heterogeneity among cells and complex biological processes. This technique reveals subtle molecular differences within individual cells, thereby offering a unique viewpoint for the investigation of cell cycle progression, cellular differentiation, and disease pathogenesis. However, accurately identifying and analyzing cell cycle dynamics in scRNA-seq data remains challenging due to the complexity of the data and
papers.summary: This paper presents SPAE, a new computational method for deciphering cell cycle dynamics and cell states from single-cell RNA-seq data. It addresses the challenge of accurately identifying cell cycle progression in complex scRNA-seq datasets, offering a tool to better understand cellular heterogeneity and biological processes.

papers.title: CellCover defines marker gene panels capturing developmental progression in neocortical neural stem cell identity.
papers.abstract: Defining cell classes is central to the analysis of growing single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlases. Marker genes are most often identified by differential expression (DE) methods that assess genes one at a time, ignoring the redundancy and complementarity revealed when genes are considered jointly. Working with binarized expression data, we instead seek discriminating panels of genes that together are specific to a cell type, framing marker-panel selection as a variant of the minimal set-covering problem in combinatorial optimization. This formulation efficiently searches the vast spac
papers.summary: CellCover is a new computational method that selects panels of marker genes for cell types by framing the problem as a minimal set-covering optimization, rather than relying on one-gene-at-a-time differential expression. Applied to neocortical neural stem cell data, it identifies gene panels that capture developmental progression and improve cell type discrimination. This approach offers a more efficient and biologically meaningful way to define cell classes in single-cell atlases.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics uncover a THBS2⁺ CAF-KRT17⁺ malignant cell axis drives progression and immunotherapy resistance in pancreatic cancer.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) features a fibrotic stroma dominated by cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), yet the functional heterogeneity of CAFs and their crosstalk with malignant cells in metastasis and immune evasion remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to characterize the tumor microenvironment of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, identifying a specific axis between THBS2-positive cancer-associated fibroblasts and KRT17-positive malignant cells that promotes tumor progression and resistance to immunotherapy. The findings reveal a novel cellular crosstalk mechanism that could serve as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: An Integrated Transcriptional and Post-Transcriptional Regulatory Circuit Orchestrated by NUDT21 Maintains the Proliferation and Survival of Neuroblastoma.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent pediatric solid tumor, associated with a poor prognosis. While alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in many cancers, its role in NB remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study identifies NUDT21 as a key regulator of alternative polyadenylation in neuroblastoma, revealing an integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional circuit that maintains tumor cell proliferation and survival. The findings highlight APA as a critical mechanism in neuroblastoma pathogenesis and a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Pasta, a Versatile Transcriptomic Clock, Maps the Chemical and Genetic Determinants of Aging and Rejuvenation.
papers.abstract: With the growing burden of age-related diseases, understanding and modulating the aging process has become a priority. Transcriptomic aging clocks (TACs) can track biological age but remain limited by platform dependence, tissue specificity, or restricted accessibility. To address this, we developed Pasta, a robust and broadly applicable human TAC, built using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework. Pasta accurately predicted relative age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-Seq as well as microarray data. Its predictions aligned with senescent and stem-lik
papers.summary: The authors developed Pasta, a new transcriptomic aging clock that uses a novel 'age-shift' learning framework to predict biological age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-Seq and microarray data. Pasta accurately tracks aging and can map chemical and genetic determinants of aging and rejuvenation, offering a versatile tool for aging research.

papers.title: Integrated Single-Nucleus Multi-Omics Atlases Reveal Lineage Plasticity and Regulatory Networks of Luminal Epithelial Cells During Mammary Gland Lactation and Involution.
papers.abstract: Dynamic changes in mammary cells are essential for sustaining lactation and maintaining epithelial homeostasis. However, the phenotypic transition process of mammary cells during lactation remains unclear. Here, single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) of 64 199 cells and single-nucleus chromatin accessibility sequencing (snATAC-seq) of 78 984 cells were generated from the goat mammary gland of dry and lactation stages. A total of 18 cell types were annotated, and spatial transcriptomic analysis confirmed the localization of lactation-related cell types within the mammary tissue. Enrichment a
papers.summary: This study generates single-nucleus multi-omics atlases (snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq) from goat mammary glands during dry and lactation stages, identifying 18 cell types and revealing lineage plasticity and regulatory networks in luminal epithelial cells. Spatial transcriptomics confirms the localization of lactation-related cell types, providing new insights into the cellular transitions underlying lactation and involution.

papers.title: Plant Immunity in High Resolution: Advances in Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics in Plant-Pathogen Interactions.
papers.abstract: Plant immune responses are shaped by cellular identity and tissue context. During interactions with pathogenic microbes, different plant cell types activate distinct defense-associated transcriptional programs that are not readily resolved using whole-tissue analyses. As a result, bulk transcriptomic approaches have limited our ability to capture spatial and cellular heterogeneity during immune responses. Recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have enabled the analysis of plant immune responses at cellular resolution while preserving spatial information. Stud
papers.summary: This review highlights how single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics are transforming the study of plant-pathogen interactions by revealing cell-type-specific immune responses that are masked in bulk tissue analyses. It discusses recent advances and their potential to capture spatial and cellular heterogeneity during plant immunity.

papers.title: The immunological landscape of the area postrema in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders.
papers.abstract: Patients suffering from aquaporin-4 antibody-positive neuromyelitis spectrum disorder may present with radically different types of lesions in the central nervous system. They may show large tissue destructive lesions, as typically seen in medulla, spinal cord, and optic nerves, and lesions with much better tissue preservation, as seen in the area postrema. The causes for the resilience of the area postrema to the action of aquaporin 4-antibodies are currently unclear. We performed detailed immunohistochemical analysis combined with spatial transcriptomics and functional annotation clustering,
papers.summary: This study investigates why the area postrema in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders (NMOSD) is more resilient to aquaporin-4 antibody-mediated damage compared to other CNS regions. Using immunohistochemistry and spatial transcriptomics, the authors characterize the unique immunological microenvironment of the area postrema, revealing cellular and molecular features that may explain its relative tissue preservation. These findings provide new insights into region-specific immune responses in NMOSD and could inform targeted therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses the emerging field of spatial biology in cancer epigenetics, highlighting how spatial transcriptomics and related technologies can reveal the spatial organization of epigenetic regulation within tumors. It emphasizes the importance of preserving tissue architecture to understand how local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs influence cancer development and progression.

papers.title: A unified developmental timeline of pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: This study presents a unified developmental timeline of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye by applying a gentle hydrogen peroxide-based bleaching method compatible with immunohistochemistry. The authors generated a detailed atlas of pigmented tissue development and re-analyzed single-cell RNA-seq data to provide a comprehensive reference for studying eye development.

papers.title: Decoding neoantigen-encoding tumor-specific transcripts unveils a shared target reservoir for immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Primary liver cancer, predominantly hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), has limited therapeutic options. While mutation-derived neoantigen vaccine holds promise, its success is hindered by low antigen availability. This study explores transcriptome-derived neoantigens (neoantigen-encoding tumor-specific transcripts, neoTSTs) in HCC, characterizing their features, generation mechanisms, and therapeutic potential.
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes neoantigen-encoding tumor-specific transcripts (neoTSTs) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), revealing a shared reservoir of transcriptome-derived neoantigens that could expand the target pool for immunotherapy. The findings suggest that neoTSTs may offer a promising alternative or complement to mutation-derived neoantigens, potentially improving vaccine efficacy in HCC.

papers.title: Autoreactive B cells in systemic lupus erythematosus: insights from integrative multi-omics analyses.
papers.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease characterized by the emergence of autoantibodies and deposition of immune complexes. SLE presents with heterogeneous multi-organ involvement that varies among patients and its mechanisms have been investigated to facilitate appropriate stratification and treatment selection. Bulk RNA-seq and bulk ATAC-seq have provided important insights into the pathogenesis of SLE; however, these approaches are inherently limited by their reliance on predefined cell subsets and known markers, which can introduce bias and restrict their ability to fu
papers.summary: This review discusses how integrative multi-omics analyses, including bulk RNA-seq and ATAC-seq, have advanced understanding of autoreactive B cells in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), while highlighting the limitations of these approaches due to reliance on predefined cell subsets. It emphasizes the need for more unbiased, single-cell-level strategies to better stratify patients and guide treatment selection.

papers.title: Robust and generalizable CNV detection for single-cell sequencing assays.
papers.abstract: Copy number variations (CNVs) are genomic structural variants that are strongly linked to cancer progression and genetic disorders. CNVs can be highly heterogeneous at population and tissue scale; thus, single-cell resolution detection holds great promise for studying clonal evolution and CNV-driven changes. Despite advanced sc-RNA-seq CNV detection methods, accurate methods for epigenomic single-cell modalities lag behind. We developed RIDDLER; a robust, unsupervised method that uses outlier-aware statistical modeling to detect CNVs across multiple single-cell modalities and assays. RIDDLER u
papers.summary: RIDDLER is a new unsupervised computational method that detects copy number variations (CNVs) in single-cell sequencing data, including epigenomic modalities where accurate detection has been lacking. It uses outlier-aware statistical modeling to achieve robust and generalizable CNV detection across multiple single-cell assays, which could improve studies of cancer clonal evolution and genetic disorders.

papers.title: Multi-Omics and Machine Learning-Based Characterization of the Lactylation Microenvironment and Biomarker Identification in Crohn's Disease Intestinal Fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Crohn's disease (CD) is characterized by transmural inflammation and intestinal fibrosis, in which metabolic reprogramming may contribute to fibrotic remodeling through lactate-associated epigenetic and transcriptional regulation, but key cellular states and candidate biomarkers remain unclear. Therefore, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with a lactylation-associated transcriptional score to estimate lactate/lactylation-related transcriptional activity in CD intestinal tissues. High-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) and an integrated machine
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing with machine learning to characterize the lactylation microenvironment in Crohn's disease intestinal fibrosis, identifying key cellular states and candidate biomarkers. The findings suggest that lactate-associated epigenetic regulation contributes to fibrotic remodeling, offering potential diagnostic and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Integrated Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals the Immunoregulatory Role of MIF Signaling in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background: The cellular heterogeneity and spatial organization patterns of the tumor microenvironment (TME) play a crucial role in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, but their spatial distribution and cellular communication mechanisms require further elucidation. This study aims to systematically dissect the cellular heterogeneity and spatial organization characteristics of the CRC microenvironment by integrating single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. Methods: Single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics data of primary CRC were integrated to characterize the TME. Intercellu
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data from colorectal cancer (CRC) to map the tumor microenvironment's cellular heterogeneity and spatial organization, revealing a key immunoregulatory role for MIF signaling in intercellular communication. The findings provide new insights into how MIF-mediated interactions may shape immune responses in CRC, offering potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Mediterranean Diet and Neurodegenerative Diseases: Recent Advances from the Gut-Immune-Brain Axis to Multi-Omics-Guided Precision Nutrition.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) are regarded as systemic illnesses, mainly characterized by long-term neuroinflammation, metabolic dysregulation and barrier dysfunction. All these factors interact through the gut-immune-brain axis. The Mediterranean diet, rich in plant-based foods, olive oil, and fish, has been consistently associated with slower cognitive decline and reduced risk of neurodegeneration in observational studies and some clinical trials. This review provides a systems-level synthesis that distinguishes itself from previous nar
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent evidence on how the Mediterranean diet influences neurodegenerative diseases through the gut-immune-brain axis, integrating multi-omics data to support precision nutrition approaches. It highlights the diet's protective effects against cognitive decline and neurodegeneration, emphasizing systemic interactions among neuroinflammation, metabolic dysregulation, and barrier dysfunction.

papers.title: Single cell CRISPR screen identifies antagonism between Nsd1-H3K36me2 and Ezh2-H3K27me3 orchestrates pluripotency transition.
papers.abstract: The transcriptional and epigenetic landscape imposes constraints on the self-renewal capacity and lineage specification potential of both naive and primed mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). CRISPR/Cas9-based functional screening coupled with single-cell RNA-seq (CROP-seq) establishes relationships between gRNA-mediated knockout genotype and transcriptome phenotype, providing a powerful tool to dissect gene regulatory networks. Here, we employed CROP-seq to investigate the epigenetic regulation governing the pluripotency network in mESCs. This highly sensitive method identified key genes essen
papers.summary: This study uses a single-cell CRISPR screen (CROP-seq) to identify epigenetic regulators essential for the pluripotency transition in mouse embryonic stem cells. The screen reveals an antagonistic relationship between Nsd1-mediated H3K36me2 and Ezh2-mediated H3K27me3 that orchestrates the switch between naive and primed pluripotency states.

papers.title: Reference Regulatory Element-Guided Gene Expression Analysis for Mechanistic Inference of Gene Regulatory Networks.
papers.abstract: Regulatory genomics faces a depth-breadth gap: deep multi-omics provides regulatory detail but is difficult to scale, whereas broad expression datasets often lack the regulatory structure needed for mechanistic Gene Regulatory Network (GRN) analysis. We developed Regulatory Elements Guided Analysis (REGA), an interpretable framework that uses reference Regulatory Element (RE) catalogs to infer transcription factor (TF)-RE-gene programs from gene expression data. Across ChIP-seq, knockdown, Hi-C, cis - and trans -eQTL benchmarks, REGA prioritized functional REs, improved RE-gene and TF-gene inf
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: REGA is a new interpretable framework that uses reference regulatory element catalogs to infer transcription factor-regulatory element-gene programs from gene expression data alone, bridging the gap between deep multi-omics and broad expression datasets. It improves the prioritization of functional regulatory elements and enhances gene regulatory network inference, as validated across multiple benchmarks including ChIP-seq, knockdown, Hi-C, and eQTL data.

papers.title: Multilayer Genomic Characterization of a Shared Genetic Factor Linking Depression-Related Liability and Reduced Physical Function.
papers.abstract: Background: Depression-related liability is frequently accompanied by reduced physical function, yet the shared genetic architecture linking mood-related traits and physical-function decline remains incompletely characterized. Methods: We applied genomic structural equation modeling to European-ancestry GWAS summary statistics for five constituent phenotypes: depressive symptoms, depression diagnosis, grip strength, appendicular lean mass, and walking pace. A Depression-Physical Function shared genetic factor was constructed as a cross-trait genetic covariance dimension and evaluated using LDS
papers.summary: This study uses genomic structural equation modeling on European-ancestry GWAS data to identify a shared genetic factor linking depression-related traits (depressive symptoms, depression diagnosis) with reduced physical function (grip strength, lean mass, walking pace). The findings reveal a common genetic architecture underlying both depression liability and physical function decline, providing insights into the pleiotropic mechanisms connecting mental and physical health.

papers.title: Spatial Topology Reveals Biologically Distinct Recurrent Motifs in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Most spatial transcriptomic analyses of solid tumors focus on individual cell states or single-sample spatial domains rather than on recurrent multicellular tissue architectures shared across patients, and typically depend on predefined cell-type annotations or compartment definitions. We developed STORM (Spatial Topology analysis of Recurrent Motifs), an unsupervised graph-attention variational autoencoder that learns recurrent spatial motifs directly from cell-level graph structure and molecular profiles without cell-type labels, manual annotation, or predefined compartments. We applied to 3
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed STORM, an unsupervised graph-attention variational autoencoder that identifies recurrent multicellular spatial motifs directly from spatial transcriptomics data without requiring cell-type labels or predefined compartments. Applied to colorectal cancer samples, STORM revealed biologically distinct recurrent tissue architectures shared across patients, offering a new approach to studying tumor organization.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics reveal mechanistic insights of FOLH1+ endothelial cells in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is the most prevalent and aggressive subtype of renal malignancy, characterized by extensive vascularization and poor prognosis. Early detection markedly improves patient outcomes, and prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA, encoded by FOLH1) imaging has recently emerged as a valuable diagnostic tool for ccRCC. However, the cellular source, spatial distribution, and mechanistic contribution of FOLH1 expression within the tumor microenvironment remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and spatial multi-omics to characterize FOLH1+ endothelial cells in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), revealing their cellular source, spatial distribution, and potential mechanistic roles in the tumor microenvironment. The findings provide new insights into how FOLH1 expression may contribute to tumor vascularization and could inform PSMA-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Scalable hypothalamic neuron differentiation from human pluripotent stem cells suitable for modeling metabolic disorders.
papers.abstract: The hypothalamus, composed of multiple nuclei, is essential for maintaining the body's homeostasis. Within the mediobasal hypothalamus, the arcuate nucleus (ARC) contains key neuronal populations, including appetite-suppressing pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons that regulate energy and glucose balance. Here, we present a chemically defined, scalable method for differentiating human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) into hypothalamic neurons enriched for POMC cells, compatible with robotic cell culture platforms for high-throughput use. Neuronal identity was validated by MERFISH single-cell tran
papers.summary: This paper presents a scalable, chemically defined method for differentiating human pluripotent stem cells into hypothalamic neurons enriched for appetite-regulating POMC neurons, compatible with robotic platforms for high-throughput screening. The method's utility for modeling metabolic disorders is supported by validation using MERFISH single-cell transcriptomics.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies a Tertiary Lymphoid Structure-Associated LAMP3+CCR7+ mregDC Antigen-Presentation Program in Ovarian Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are spatial immune niches in solid tumors, but their relationship to mature regulatory dendritic-cell (mregDC) states in ovarian cancer remains incompletely resolved. Methods: We integrated public gynecological-tumor single-cell RNA sequencing, representative CD11C/HLA-DRA/LAMP3/CCR7 multiplex immunofluorescence, public Xenium and multi-sample spatial transcriptomics, TCGA-OV immune deconvolution and exploratory prognostic modeling, scTenifoldKnk and CellOracle perturbation analyses, and supplementary computational drug prioritization. Results: A
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to identify a LAMP3+CCR7+ mature regulatory dendritic cell (mregDC) population associated with tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) in ovarian cancer, revealing a potential antigen-presentation program linked to TLS formation. The findings suggest that this mregDC subset may play a role in shaping the tumor immune microenvironment and could inform prognostic or therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-Transcriptomic Uncovers Actionable Signatures and Drug Repurposing Candidates for ccRCC-Hypertension Comorbidity.
papers.abstract: Hypertension is a common comorbidity and risk factor for clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), yet the molecular mechanisms linking these two diseases remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate hypertension-related molecular signatures in ccRCC using integrated multi-transcriptomic analyses.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated multi-transcriptomic analyses to identify molecular signatures linking hypertension and clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), and proposes drug repurposing candidates for this comorbidity. The findings provide potential actionable targets and therapeutic options for ccRCC patients with hypertension.

papers.title: Functional Depth Biomarkers Distinguish Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma from Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) exhibit fundamentally distinct pathway coordination architectures. We developed a framework integrating pathway activity inference from spatial transcriptomics data, spatial proximity based network construction, and functional depth analysis across 996 TCGA patients. Applying Fraiman-Muniz depth statistics, we generated two representations: Population Referenced Depth quantifies typicality relative to population distributions, while Patient Referenced Depth assesses within-patient network organization. Random forest classificat
papers.summary: This study introduces a framework that integrates spatial transcriptomics pathway activity, spatial proximity networks, and functional depth analysis to distinguish lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) from lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Using Fraiman-Muniz depth statistics on TCGA data, the authors generate population- and patient-referenced depth representations, which when used with random forest classification, effectively differentiate the two cancer subtypes based on pathway coordination architecture.

papers.title: Identification of potential diagnostic biomarkers for myocardial infarction using bioinformatics and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Acute myocardial infarction(AMI)is an important type of cardiovascular disease, which seriously threatens the lives of humans. In order to help patients receive timely clinical treatment and improve their survival rates, it is necessary to screen out related molecules in advance. To this end, we applied bioinformatics methods and machine learning algorithms to find possible biomarkers associated with AMI. When considering possible connections with dynamics of immune cells activation. Based on the RNA-seq results, differential expression analysis was performed followed by WGCNA to identify stab
papers.summary: This study uses bioinformatics and machine learning to identify potential diagnostic biomarkers for acute myocardial infarction (AMI), with a focus on immune cell dynamics. The authors performed differential expression analysis and WGCNA on RNA-seq data to find candidate genes that could aid in early diagnosis and improve patient outcomes.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics identifies CYP1B1 as a candidate molecular link between toxicant exposure and ferroptosis-related epithelial stress in COPD.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by progressive airflow limitation, chronic airway inflammation, and epithelial remodeling. Although oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation are increasingly recognized as important contributors to COPD pathobiology, the epithelial biomarkers and regulatory pathways linking cigarette-smoke exposure to ferroptosis-related injury remain incompletely defined.
papers.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
papers.summary: This study uses an integrative multi-omics approach to identify CYP1B1 as a potential molecular link between toxicant exposure (e.g., cigarette smoke) and ferroptosis-related epithelial stress in COPD. The findings suggest that CYP1B1 may serve as a biomarker and therapeutic target for COPD, connecting environmental exposure to a specific cell death pathway.

papers.title: PathwayBench: a multi-criterion benchmark of pseudobulk pathway activity scoring methods reveals rank-window competition as a mechanism of biological signal loss in single-cell RNA-seq.
papers.abstract: Pathway activity scoring is a foundational step in single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) analysis, yet method choice is rarely guided by systematic, multi-criterion evidence in the pseudobulk case-control regime that now dominates applied single-cell disease studies. Prior single-cell pathway-scoring benchmarks have focused on perturbation ground truth at cell-level resolution, leaving the donor-level pseudobulk setting - and the question of why methods disagree - largely unaddressed.
papers.summary: This paper introduces PathwayBench, a multi-criterion benchmark for evaluating pseudobulk pathway activity scoring methods in single-cell RNA-seq case-control studies. The authors identify 'rank-window competition' as a mechanism causing biological signal loss, providing systematic evidence to guide method selection in this common analytical setting.

papers.title: T Cell-Macrophage Interactions Influence Chemotherapeutic Response in Ovarian Cancer Patients.
papers.abstract: Tumour development and progression involve complex cell-cell interactions and dynamic co-evolution between cancer cells, immune cells and stromal cells in the tumour microenvironment and this may influence therapeutic resistance. A large proportion of this network relies on direct physical interactions between cells, particularly T-cell mediated interactions. Cell-cell communication inference has now become routine in downstream scRNAseq analysis but this mostly fails to capture physical cell-cell interactions due to tissue dissociation. Doublets occur naturally in scRNA-seq and are usually ex
papers.summary: This study investigates how physical T cell-macrophage interactions in the tumor microenvironment influence chemotherapeutic response in ovarian cancer, using scRNA-seq doublets as a proxy for direct cell-cell contacts. The findings suggest that these specific immune cell interactions may play a role in therapeutic resistance, offering potential insights for improving treatment strategies.

papers.title: KNOX1 Transcription Factors in Plants with a Special Focus on Horticultural Crops: A Review.
papers.abstract: Class I KNOX1 (KNOTTED1-like homeobox 1) transcription factors integrate gibberellin (GA), cytokinin (CK), and auxin (IAA) signaling to maintain shoot apical meristem identity and coordinate plant organogenesis. This review examines the structural conservation, evolutionary dynamics, and regulatory architecture of KNOX1 genes across horticultural crops, drawing essential mechanistic context from model species. We synthesize KNOX1 functions in six agronomic domains, including plant architecture and branching, leaf morphogenesis and ornamental traits, floral development and sex determination, fr
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on Class I KNOX1 transcription factors, focusing on their roles in hormone signaling integration and organogenesis, with an emphasis on horticultural crops. It covers structural conservation, evolutionary dynamics, and regulatory functions across six agronomic domains, providing a valuable resource for understanding and potentially manipulating plant architecture and development in crop improvement.

papers.title: Reappraising Kidney Biopsy in Diabetic Kidney Disease: Histopathology, Clinical Course, and the Future of Precision Nephrology.
papers.abstract: Background: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is one of the leading causes of chronic kidney disease and kidney failure worldwide. Although most patients with diabetes are diagnosed clinically on the basis of albuminuria, estimated glomerular filtration rate decline, and diabetic retinopathy, clinical parameters alone may not reliably distinguish biopsy-proven diabetic nephropathy (DN) from non-diabetic kidney disease (NDKD) or mixed lesions. The role of kidney biopsy in diabetic patients therefore remains selective rather than routine, but its diagnostic and prognostic value is increasingly relev
papers.summary: This review discusses the role of kidney biopsy in diabetic kidney disease, highlighting that clinical parameters alone may not reliably distinguish diabetic nephropathy from non-diabetic kidney disease or mixed lesions. It emphasizes the diagnostic and prognostic value of histopathology and the potential for precision nephrology approaches in the future.

papers.title: Counterfactual Diffusion Modeling Enables Spatially Targeted Reprogramming of Tissue Microenvironments.
papers.abstract: Spatially resolved single-cell technologies can provide deep insights into cellular heterogeneity and tissue structural characteristics. However, the data obtained are purely observational and cannot reveal the specific mechanisms by which tissues respond to particular perturbations. Most computational models of single-cell perturbations either operate in a non-spatial latent space or fix tissue geometry within a static spatial structure, thereby limiting their ability to integrate molecular profiles with tissue topological remodeling. We propose SPAD-CFR (Spatial Point-cloud Attention-based D
papers.summary: This paper introduces SPAD-CFR, a counterfactual diffusion model that predicts how spatial transcriptomics data would change under perturbations while allowing tissue structure to remodel, not just molecular profiles. It addresses a key limitation of existing perturbation models by integrating molecular changes with tissue topological dynamics, enabling spatially targeted reprogramming predictions.

papers.title: PLNFGL: joint estimation of multi-condition gene networks from single-cell RNA-seq data.
papers.abstract: Graphical models have been widely used in bioinformatics to infer the conditional dependence structure among random variables, but traditional Gaussian graphical models (GGMs) are suboptimal for single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) due to dropout events and distributional mismatch. Moreover, most existing methods estimate networks under a single condition, limiting their utility in multi-condition studies.
papers.summary: This paper introduces PLNFGL, a new computational method for jointly estimating gene regulatory networks across multiple biological conditions from single-cell RNA-seq data. It addresses limitations of traditional Gaussian graphical models by accounting for dropout events and distributional mismatches in scRNA-seq, enabling more accurate multi-condition network inference.

papers.title: Identifying condition-related cell-cell communication events using supervised tensor analysis.
papers.abstract: Many tools have been developed to infer active cell-cell communication (CCC) events, which are essential for understanding biological processes and diseases. However, existing methods for assessing the relationships between CCC events and biological conditions have at least one practical limitation: a lack of clear interpretation, an inability to adjust for confounders, or an inability to model inherent dependencies among CCC events. To comprehensively address these limitations, we introduce STACCato, a supervised tensor analysis tool for identifying condition-related CCC events. STACCato empl
papers.summary: The paper introduces STACCato, a supervised tensor analysis tool that identifies cell-cell communication events associated with biological conditions while addressing limitations of existing methods, such as lack of interpretability, inability to adjust for confounders, and failure to model dependencies among events. STACCato provides a comprehensive approach to link CCC events to conditions, potentially improving disease-related studies.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomic analysis reveals spatial features in human Stanford type A aortic dissection.
papers.abstract: Stanford type A aortic dissection (AAD) is a life-threatening cardiovascular disease characterized by tearing in the aortic wall. Using spatial transcriptomics and multiplex immunofluorescence, we comprehensively analyzed ascending aortas from eight AAD patients across different severities and segments. We demonstrate that SPP1-driven inflammatory signaling intensifies with AAD severity, identifying a nine-gene, layer-anchored severity scale: MYL6/CALD1/MYH9 (mild); CCL2/CP/COL4A1 (moderate); and TMSB4X/ATP5F1E/PKM (severe). Importantly, the collagen-remodeling triad COL1A1/COL3A1/MMP2 is conc
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics and multiplex immunofluorescence to map gene expression across ascending aortas from eight patients with Stanford type A aortic dissection (AAD), revealing that SPP1-driven inflammatory signaling intensifies with disease severity. The authors identify a nine-gene, layer-anchored severity scale (mild, moderate, severe) and highlight a collagen-remodeling triad (COL1A1/COL3A1/MMP2) as a key feature, providing new spatial insights into AAD pathology.

papers.title: Multiomics identifies a prognostic signature and SPIB as a potential regulator of gastric cancer lymph node metastasis.
papers.abstract: The heterogeneity within the same AJCC TNM stage of gastric cancer necessitates robust prognostic biomarkers beyond conventional staging. By integrating transcriptomic data from 1,613 patients across eight cohorts, we developed an 11-gene lymph node metastasis gene signature (LMGS) using an ensemble learning strategy to overcome the instability of traditional models. LMGS robustly predicted survival (mean C-index = 0.619), providing incremental prognostic value beyond conventional AJCC staging. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses revealed LMGS enrichment in epithelial/immune cells
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data from 1,613 gastric cancer patients to develop an 11-gene lymph node metastasis signature (LMGS) that predicts survival more accurately than conventional staging. Using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, the authors identify SPIB as a potential regulator of lymph node metastasis, offering new insights into gastric cancer biology and potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Ligand-based directed differentiation to produce granulosa-like cells expressing steroidogenic enzyme genes.
papers.abstract: The ovarian granulosa cells are responsible for producing hormones and supporting oocytes through maturation and meiotic resumption. There is a need to generate granulosa-like cells (GLCs) from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) to better model human gonadal development and to test the effects of exogenous or pharmaceutical compounds on the ovary. Here we report a rapid ligand-based protocol for differentiating hiPSCs into cells that express markers of the transient developmental lineages and steroidogenic pathway genes. Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis identified can
papers.summary: This paper describes a new ligand-based protocol to rapidly differentiate human induced pluripotent stem cells into granulosa-like cells that express steroidogenic enzyme genes, providing a useful in vitro model for studying ovarian development and testing pharmaceutical effects. The authors used single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize the differentiated cells and confirm their identity.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics supports a role for SOX4-driven signaling throughout the disease course of biliary atresia.
papers.abstract: Biliary atresia (BA) is a neonatal fibroinflammatory cholangiopathy of infancy and the most common indication for pediatric liver transplantation. We aimed to define the molecular mechanisms responsible for differences in the rate of disease progression among children with BA.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to investigate biliary atresia (BA), a neonatal liver disease, and identifies SOX4-driven signaling as a key pathway active throughout the disease course. The findings suggest that SOX4 may contribute to the variable progression rates seen in BA patients, offering a potential target for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Single Cell and Spatially Resolved Transcriptome and Immune Repertoire of Mouse Thymus During Aging Reveal Immunological Heterogeneity and Direction of Thymic Selection Pressure.
papers.abstract: The thymus is the central organ where T cells differentiate and proliferate. T cells experience the TCR recombination to generate diversity, self-antigen tolerance, and immune response. However, the spatial heterogeneity of transcriptomics and immune repertoire of the thymus during aging haven't been studied. We constructed the thymus's spatial transcriptomics and spatial immune repertoire atlas by TCR-specific amplification. The integrated multi-omics analysis of the scRNA-seq, ST-seq, spatial-TCR-seq, scTCR-seq, and TCR-seq was developed to investigate the thymus during aging. ST-seq demonst
papers.summary: This study constructs a comprehensive spatial and single-cell transcriptomic and immune repertoire atlas of the mouse thymus across aging, revealing immunological heterogeneity and changes in thymic selection pressure. By integrating multiple omics approaches, the authors uncover how aging alters the thymic microenvironment and T cell development, providing new insights into age-related immune decline.

papers.title: Discovery of hub genes linking oxidative stress to type 2 diabetic sarcopenia using single-cell sequencing and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and sarcopenia demonstrate a significant comorbidity, particularly in the elderly, yet the molecular mechanisms linking them, especially through oxidative stress, remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify oxidative stress-related hub genes involved in T2DM-associated sarcopenia (T2DS) by integrating single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and bulk RNA-seq data with machine learning. We analyzed scRNA-seq datasets (GSE244515, GSE268953) to characterize cellular heterogeneity and bulk RNA-seq datasets (GSE202295, GSE226151) for differential expre
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing with machine learning to identify oxidative stress-related hub genes that may link type 2 diabetes mellitus and sarcopenia. The findings provide candidate molecular targets and insights into the shared pathophysiology of these comorbid conditions in the elderly.

papers.title: Gut microbiota induces immune-related alterations in gene expression, RNA methylation, and metabolism in glioblastoma revealed by single-cell and spatial multi-omics.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly malignant tumor with poor prognosis and limited effective treatment options. Emerging studies have suggested that gut microbiota may influence glioma progression through the gut-brain axis, though the precise mechanisms remain largely unclear. In this study, we employed a comprehensive multi-omics approach-encompassing single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, metagenomics, metabolomics, and m6A-seq-to investigate how antibiotic-induced gut microbiota disruption impacts glioma progression in a mouse model. Gene expression analysis revealed significant
papers.summary: This study uses a multi-omics approach to show that antibiotic-induced gut microbiota disruption alters gene expression, RNA methylation, and metabolism in a mouse model of glioblastoma, revealing potential gut-brain axis mechanisms. The findings suggest that the gut microbiome may influence glioma progression through immune-related changes, offering new insights into potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Analysis of senescence in pituitary tumors from different lineages and the potential role of senolytic drugs as targeted therapies.
papers.abstract: Pituitary tumors (PT) constitute the second most frequent intracranial tumor. A subset of PT can behave aggressively despite multimodal treatment. Hallmarks such as cellular senescence, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and stemness have been implicated in tumor progression, but their role in PT pathogenesis remains is unclear.
papers.summary: This study analyzes markers of cellular senescence, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and stemness in pituitary tumors across different lineages, finding lineage-specific patterns and suggesting that senolytic drugs could be a targeted therapeutic approach for aggressive cases. The findings highlight the potential of senescence as a therapeutic vulnerability in pituitary tumors.

papers.title: A multi-omics framework integrating gut microbiota, blood metabolites, and immune cells to elucidate the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) develops through complex interactions between the central nervous system and peripheral systems. The microbiota-metabolite-immune axis has emerged as an important focus of AD research. However, the coordinated mechanisms that regulate this axis remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study uses a multi-omics approach to integrate gut microbiota, blood metabolites, and immune cells, revealing coordinated mechanisms along the microbiota-metabolite-immune axis that contribute to Alzheimer's disease pathogenesis. The findings provide a systems-level view of how peripheral factors may influence AD development.

papers.title: From proteome-wide Mendelian randomization and multi-omics integration to functional validation: TGFB3 as a prioritized candidate in gastric adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Gastric adenocarcinoma lacks robust circulating biomarkers and tractable targets. We assessed whether genetically predicted plasma protein levels influence disease risk and sought druggable candidates using a proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) framework.
papers.summary: This study uses proteome-wide Mendelian randomization to identify plasma proteins that may influence gastric adenocarcinoma risk, integrating multi-omics data and functional validation to prioritize TGFB3 as a candidate biomarker and potential drug target. The findings suggest TGFB3 could be a tractable target for gastric cancer, though further validation is needed.

papers.title: Global research landscape and trends of single-cell sequencing in sexually transmitted infections: a comprehensive bibliometric analysis from 2015 to 2025.
papers.abstract: Single-cell sequencing offers new insights into sexually transmitted infections (STIs) research, but there remains a lack of systematic bibliometric overview. Here, we summarize and quantify the developmental dynamics, research hotspots, and future directions of single-cell sequencing in STIs through bibliometric analysis.
papers.summary: This paper provides a bibliometric analysis of single-cell sequencing research applied to sexually transmitted infections (STIs) from 2015 to 2025, mapping publication trends, key contributors, and emerging research hotspots. It highlights the growing application of single-cell technologies to understand STI pathogenesis and identifies future directions for the field.

papers.title: A deep learning representation and spatial Bayesian cell-type deconvolution for spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics provides unprecedented insights into gene expression in the spatial context of tissues; however, some mainstream techniques lack quantitative analysis of uncertainty.
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning-based representation and a spatial Bayesian method for cell-type deconvolution in spatial transcriptomics, addressing the lack of uncertainty quantification in existing approaches. The method improves cell-type identification accuracy and provides confidence estimates, enhancing the reliability of spatial gene expression analyses.
